correctness.rationale: From the Picard-rank-two pole-order bases, the complete Cox ring is the monic Weierstrass hypersurface in five generators. Direct computation of all five partial derivatives, split at z=0 versus z invertible, proves the reduced singular support P union L; the squarefree discriminant ensures no other critical points over nonzero base vectors. Weighted blowup of the degree-six cone yields a single smooth genus-one exceptional curve of degree -1 and Milnor number 10. The isolated weighted degree 6 chi threefold slice has Jacobian algebra dimension 2(6chi-1)^2. The nonconstant j has genuine poles at discriminant roots. Sample computations were executed successfully and do not replace the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The older literature proves the elliptic surface is Mori dream; the newer 18 November 2026 primary paper explicitly establishes the same Cox hypersurface presentation but not its full two-component singular support, transverse Milnor invariants, or varying analytic type. Classical simple-elliptic theory concerns normal surfaces rather than the full Cox-space strata. Direct targeted literature searches and two accessible recent claim ledgers found no equivalent mathematical implication. An implicit derivation from existing presentations is a remaining priority risk.
residual_risks: The algebra presentation became publicly available on 18 November 2026, after the 15 November 2026 source-cohort anchor; it is therefore comparison literature, not the dated seed.
Unindexed papers or general theorems on singularities of spectra of Cox rings could implicitly give all or part of the result.
The classification is set-theoretic and does not extend to discriminant-plane slices or the intersection origin.

value.rationale: The geometric object is the natural total coordinate space of the Picard-two Mori-dream elliptic surfaces. A global plane-plus-line singular support and the sharply different transverse invariants (one elliptic surface slice with continuously varying j at fixed Milnor ten; another isolated threefold slice with 2(6chi−1)^2) describe precisely how the fibration geometry persists in the Cox space. The combined structural insight is not a finite arbitrary parameter substitution or a re-listing of Cox generators.
